subject: Priority deletion windows + confirmation that customer data is not used for model training
messages:
From: Rebecca Lang <rebecca.lang@finservcorp.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: security@finservcorp.com
Date: 2025-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: priority deletion windows + training assurance

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Two follow-ups from FinServ security:

1) We need a clear operational timeline for a 'priority deletion' request — our legal team wants to know how deletion propagates through live caches, debug snapshots, backups, and any cross-region replicas. In particular, what parts of the stack are considered 'immediately erased' vs 'marked for deletion and removed on the next compaction'?

2) Your security contact mentioned that Redwood does not use customer request data to train models. Can you provide the exact language we can include in our procurement docs (and an explanation of edge cases: e.g., debug snapshots, telemetry, or derived heuristics)?

If you can send an operations-level explanation plus a short customer-facing sentence we can include in the contract, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Rebecca
Security + Privacy
FinServCorp

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lang <rebecca.lang@finservcorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: priority deletion windows + training assurance

Hi Rebecca — thank you, and great questions. Below is an operational summary (intended for your security/ops team) followed by a one-sentence customer clause you can paste into procurement. I'll attach the ops runbook as well.

Operational summary (high level):
- Immediate actions (seconds to minutes):
  - Primary tenant data is removed from live serving stores and request-level logs are tombstoned. Active KV caches are invalidated for the affected tenant and keys are evicted; in-flight requests that reference the data are allowed to complete but the data is not stored thereafter.
- Short-term propagation (minutes to hours):
  - In-memory caches and worker-level KV stores are cleared asynchronously. Persistent debug snapshots created for ongoing troubleshooting are flagged and scheduled for secure deletion within the same maintenance window (our default priority window is 24–72 hours depending on workload).
- Backups & replicas (hours to up to 30 days depending on retention tier):
  - Regular backup snapshots are immutable; we maintain a tombstone-and-expunge workflow. For priority deletes we accelerate the expunge lifecycle for affected shards and mark associated backups for early rekeying/rotation and purging where possible. For legal holds, we provide a custodian workflow instead of deletion.
- Audit & evidence:
  - Every step is recorded in our erase audit trail (timestamped events, operator IDs, and job IDs). We can produce attestations and a timeline of the ops we ran for the account.

Edge cases / clarifications:
- Debug snapshots: transient debug artifacts (created for a specific incident) are treated as ephemeral; when a priority delete is requested we schedule immediate secure wipe and record the wipe event. If a snapshot is part of an immutable backup set older than the expunge window, we follow the backup purge acceleration process and provide proof of purge where possible.
- Telemetry / aggregated metrics: we do not retain identifiable customer text in aggregated telemetry used for system health and capacity planning. Any telemetry containing sample inputs is redacted before being used in product analytics.
- Derived heuristics or feature flags: feature usage signals (booleans/counters) are stored without customer text and are not used to train generative models.

Training assurance (customer-facing clause):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer-provided content, prompts, or outputs to train or improve our machine learning models. Customer data is isolated from open training pipelines; any telemetry used for product health is aggregated and redacted to remove customer-identifying content."

I'll loop in Ben to provide the erase runbook and expected SLAs for the accelerated expunge path.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lang <rebecca.lang@finservcorp.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: priority deletion windows + training assurance

Rebecca — attaching our erase runbook (PDF) and a short guidance text file for our engineering team that describes debug-snapshot lifecycle. TL;DR on timelines and SLAs we offer for priority deletes:

- Priority delete processing: initial tombstone and cache eviction within 0–2 hours for hosted accounts on Dedicated nodes; full expunge from hot storage typically within 24 hours; backups purged or rotated within 3–30 days depending on backup tier and retention policy.
- Evidence package: We can provide an export with timestamps, job IDs, and SHA256 of purged objects where feasible.
- SLA addendum: For priority delete requests under an enterprise agreement (Deal FS-2025-0892) Redwood will commit to a documented accelerated expunge timeline and provide periodic attestation until the purge is complete.

Notes about training & model pipelines (ops detail):
- Our inference pipeline separates serving telemetry and training corpora. Serving logs and request payloads are stored in tenant-scoped buckets; unless a customer opts into a data-sharing program (explicit contract clause), those buckets are excluded from our model-training ingestion pipelines.
- We do keep short-lived debug traces for debugging prod incidents; these traces are time-limited and, for priority deletion requests, we run an expedited secure-wipe job that removes traces and logs tied to the tenant.

Attachments:
- erase_runbook_v2.pdf (contains runbook, expunge job IDs, operator checklist)
- debug-snapshot-guidance.txt (short operations note)

If you need a redlineable SLA paragraph or a joint statement for procurement, let us know and Marissa can pull the contractual language.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: Rebecca Lang <rebecca.lang@finservcorp.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: security@finservcorp.com

Thanks Mina / Ben — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick asks before we close the thread:

- Rebecca (legal) asked for that single customer-facing sentence as a short paragraph for the procurement doc; the wording you provided is acceptable, but can we add a parenthetical to make explicit that "model training" excludes telemetry that is aggregated and redacted? Suggestion: append "(excluding aggregated and redacted telemetry used for product health)".
- Can you provide an example evidence package (redacted) so our audit folks can see the schema? If possible, drop it into the Drive link you sent.

If you can confirm those two items I will route to procurement and we can sign the SLA addendum for FS-2025-0892.

Regards,
Rebecca Lang
Security + Privacy
FinServCorp
